agenda: The situation in the Middle East; Report of the Secretary-General on the United Nations Disengagement Observer Force (S/2025/350)
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: Our primary objective as co-penholder with the United States is to secure a smooth six-month renewal of UNDOF's mandate until 31 December 2025, preserving the established balance and strict adherence to the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. We anticipate delicate negotiations surrounding characterizations of the recent political and military developments on the Bravo side following the transition in Damascus, as well as pushback if Western members attempt to introduce unbalanced language regarding Syrian sovereignty or Israeli incursions into the area of separation. Maintaining the consensus text and keeping UNDOF focused strictly on its mandate and the safety of peacekeepers remain our guiding priorities.

messages.Algeria: Algeria thanks the co-penholders for their efforts in preparing the draft resolution extending UNDOF's mandate, which is vital for regional stability. Given the dangerous developments on the ground and repeated violations across the ceasefire line, the resolution must explicitly uphold Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity. It is equally imperative to clearly call for an end to military incursions and the complete withdrawal of all unauthorized military forces from the area of separation in strict accordance with the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement.
messages.China: China supports the draft resolution extending the mandate of UNDOF for a period of six months as circulated by the co-penholders. UNDOF plays an indispensable role in maintaining stability between Israel and Syria and upholding the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. We appreciate the constructive efforts of the Russian Federation and the United States in facilitating consensus, and we look forward to the timely adoption of the text.
messages.Denmark: Denmark fully supports the draft resolution renewing UNDOF's mandate for a further six months and commends the co-penholders for their constructive joint leadership in preserving Council unity on this file. UNDOF remains an essential stabilizing presence in the region, and we underscore the critical importance of ensuring the safety, security, and unhindered freedom of movement of its peacekeepers. We welcome the continuation of strong language regarding the implementation of the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, performance frameworks, and the women, peace, and security agenda.
messages.France: France fully supports the draft resolution extending the mandate of UNDOF for six months. In a volatile regional context, the presence of UNDOF remains vital for maintaining stability and upholding the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. We commend the co-penholders for maintaining a balanced and consensual text and look forward to its unanimous adoption.
messages.Greece: Greece welcomes the draft resolution renewing the mandate of UNDOF and expresses appreciation to the co-penholders for maintaining a constructive, consensus-based approach. We reiterate our steadfast support for UNDOF’s indispensable role in preserving stability, monitoring the ceasefire, and preventing escalation along the Golan. Ensuring the safety, security, and unhindered freedom of movement of peacekeepers remains of paramount importance, and Greece stands ready to support the adoption of the text as drafted.
messages.Guyana: Guyana thanks the co-penholders, the Russian Federation and the United States, for circulating this balanced draft resolution. We fully support the six-month renewal of UNDOF's mandate, which remains indispensable for maintaining the ceasefire and regional stability. We also reiterate our strong commitment to the safety, security, and freedom of movement of UN peacekeepers operating in an increasingly complex environment.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan fully supports the draft resolution extending the mandate of UNDOF for an additional six months. As a leading troop-contributing country, we attach the utmost importance to the safety, security, and unhindered operational capacity of UN peacekeepers, as well as regular and meaningful consultations with TCCs. We commend the co-penholders for preserving Council unity on this essential mission to maintain regional stability.
messages.Panama: Panama fully supports the draft resolution renewing the mandate of UNDOF for a period of six months. We commend the co-penholders for preserving a balanced and constructive text that maintains stability in the region while safeguarding the security and operational capability of United Nations personnel. Panama stands ready to vote in favour of the draft as currently circulated.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea expresses its full support for the draft resolution renewing the mandate of UNDOF for an additional six months. We thank the co-penholders, the Russian Federation and the United States, for their balanced draft, which appropriately emphasizes the safety and security of peacekeepers, mission performance, and full compliance with the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. At this critical juncture in the region, UNDOF's continued presence and impartial monitoring role remain essential for regional peace and stability.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone fully supports the draft resolution extending the mandate of UNDOF until 31 December 2025. We commend the co-penholders for maintaining a balanced and constructive text that prioritizes the safety, security, and operational readiness of peacekeepers, while reaffirming support for Force Commander Major General Anita Asmah. Sierra Leone stands ready to support the text as drafted.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia fully supports the draft resolution extending the mandate of UNDOF for an additional six months. The text strikes the right balance in reaffirming the crucial stabilizing role of UNDOF, ensuring the safety and security of peacekeepers, and urging all parties to respect the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. We appreciate the efforts of the co-penholders to maintain consensus on this critical mission.
messages.Somalia: Somalia fully supports the draft resolution renewing UNDOF's mandate for an additional six months. We commend the co-penholders for presenting a balanced text that ensures the safety, security, and operational effectiveness of UN peacekeepers while promoting stability in the region. Somalia stands ready to vote in favor of the resolution as drafted.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom fully supports the draft resolution renewing UNDOF's mandate for a further six months and thanks the co-penholders, the United States and the Russian Federation, for maintaining consensus on this vital mission. UNDOF continues to play an indispensable role in preserving stability between Israel and Syria and upholding the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement during a critical time for regional security. We pay tribute to the dedication and service of UNDOF peacekeepers and Observer Group Golan personnel who continue to carry out their duties under increasingly complex and demanding conditions.
messages.United States of America: As co-penholder, the United States strongly supports this draft resolution to renew UNDOF's mandate for an additional six months. The text reflects a carefully balanced rollover that ensures UNDOF retains the necessary mandate, force protection, and resources to monitor the ceasefire and maintain stability. We urge all Council members to preserve the consensus on this critical mission and adopt the resolution unanimously.

replies.Algeria: rejected: Preserving the established and carefully negotiated consensus between the co-penholders is essential for Council unity, and the eighth preambular paragraph already underscores that no unauthorized military forces or equipment should be present in the area of separation.

steps.summary: As co-penholder alongside the United States, the Russian Federation maintained the balanced technical rollover text without modifications to safeguard broad consensus and Council unity on UNDOF's mandate renewal. Algeria's proposed additions were declined because the prohibition on unauthorized military presence in the area of separation is already reaffirmed in the preamble, and opening agreed language could disrupt mission consensus. Unanimous adoption by the Security Council is expected.

messages.Algeria: Algeria regrets that our proposals reaffirming the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic and addressing unauthorized military presence in the area of separation were not incorporated into the draft. Nevertheless, recognizing the vital role UNDOF plays in maintaining stability and the importance of Council consensus on this file, Algeria supports the draft resolution and will vote in favour. We will place on record in our statement our principled position regarding scrupulous compliance with the 1974 Disengagement Agreement and respect for Syrian sovereignty.

steps.summary: All Council members have confirmed their full support for the draft resolution renewing UNDOF's mandate until 31 December 2025 without further amendments. As co-penholder, the Russian Federation maintains the consensual text of Revision 1, which preserves stability and operational continuity on the Golan. The draft resolution is placed in blue and is expected to be adopted unanimously (15-0-0).

after.Algeria:
I would like to begin by expressing our gratitude to the co-penholders, the Russian Federation and the United States, for their constructive efforts that have led to the unanimous renewal of the mandate of the United Nations Disengagement Observer Force (UNDOF).

Algeria voted in favour of the resolution because of the vital role UNDOF continues to play in maintaining stability and preserving the ceasefire at this critical juncture for Syria and the wider Middle East. We pay tribute to the military and civilian personnel of UNDOF and the Observer Group Golan, as well as the troop-contributing countries, for their dedication and service in a challenging operating environment.

In this context, Algeria wishes to reiterate the following key points:

First, the resolution clearly underscores that there should be no military forces, military equipment, or personnel in the area of separation other than those of UNDOF. Any military presence, incursion, or establishment of military positions by the Israeli occupying forces in the area of separation constitutes a flagrant breach of the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, the ceasefire, and relevant Security Council resolutions. Such illegal acts must cease immediately, and all forces must withdraw from the area of separation.

Secondly, the 1974 Disengagement Agreement remains legally binding and cannot be altered unilaterally. Both parties are obligated to scrupulously respect its provisions and exercise maximum restraint. The repeated violations of the ceasefire and the strikes carried out across the ceasefire line undermine regional stability and jeopardize the safety of United Nations peacekeepers, whose security, freedom of movement, and access must be fully respected and guaranteed.

Finally, Algeria reaffirms its steadfast commitment to the sovereignty, unity, independence, and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic. We recall that the Syrian Golan is occupied Syrian territory and reiterate Security Council resolution 497 (1981), which declared the Israeli decision to impose its laws, jurisdiction, and administration in the occupied Syrian Golan null and void and without international legal effect. 

The mandate of UNDOF is a temporary arrangement and cannot be a substitute for a just, comprehensive, and lasting peace in the Middle East based on relevant Security Council resolutions, including resolution 338 (1973), and the complete end to the occupation of all Arab lands.

I thank you.
after.Russian Federation:
The Russian Federation welcomes the unanimous adoption of the resolution extending the mandate of the United Nations Disengagement Observer Force (UNDOF) for another six months.

As co-penholder on this file together with the United States, we express our gratitude to all members of the Security Council for their constructive engagement and for maintaining unity on this important resolution. 

UNDOF continues to play an indispensable stabilizing role in the Golan, particularly against the backdrop of heightened tensions and serious security challenges across the region. We reaffirm our full support for the Mission’s leadership and personnel, as well as the military observers of the United Nations Truce Supervision Organization assigned to Observer Group Golan, who perform their duties under challenging and often dangerous conditions.

We reiterate that strict compliance by both parties with the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement is essential. There must be no military activity or military presence in the area of separation other than that of UNDOF peacekeepers. Any violation of the ceasefire line and the buffer zone risks undermining regional stability and jeopardizing the safety of United Nations personnel. 

Russia consistently upholds the fundamental principles of international law, the relevant Security Council resolutions, and the unwavering necessity of respecting the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic. We expect that UNDOF will continue to carry out its mandate in full, and we call on all parties to extend their full cooperation to the Mission to ensure its freedom of movement and the safety and security of its personnel.
